Liam: Hey team — first morning! Quick question: can someone point me to the 'who to message for X' cheat sheet?
Anya: Welcome Liam! Short answer: access issues -> #eng-infra, hardware/badge -> #people-ops, customer escalations -> #support. There's a pinned 'routing map' in #new-hires.
Liam: thanks — also got pinged a ton by PR bots. What's the clean way to reduce noise but still get important alerts?
InfraBot: Tip: use `@InfraBot subscribe --only=assigned` to only receive infra alerts you're subscribed to. For channel-level adjustments, Channel name -> Notifications -> Customize -> Mute app notifications. Do not mute #incidents or #eng-oncall.
Anya: If a bot keeps spamming, @mention the owner in-thread asking for rate-limits. Ops prefers keeping the conversation in-thread so context is preserved.
Liam: Any recommended intro format to post in team channels?
Anya: Keep it micro: "Liam | he/him | Platform | PST | Focus: autoscaling | Fun: baker." Post that in #new-hires and add a 1-liner to your team channel.
Liam: Sweet. I'm remote — how to set DND but allow oncall pings?
Anya: Preferences -> Notifications -> Do Not Disturb. Use `/dnd schedule 22:00 07:00` and then add channel exceptions in the channel settings for #eng-oncall if you want to allow oncall pings. Or use `@oncall-bot subscribe override` for explicit overrides.
People-Ops: Badge and equipment requests: use the Equipment form linked in #people-ops. Standard turnaround is 48 hours; choose 'expedite' for urgent.
Liam: Are there places where we should never paste credentials or full stack traces?
Anya: Never paste secrets in channels. Use secure gist or drive links and redact tokens. For stack traces, paste minimal failing frames and link to the full log.
onboarding-buddy: Hey Liam — I DM'd the checklist and calendar invites. We'll run through channel etiquette at 3pm PT.
Liam: thanks everyone — super clear. Saved the pinned links. :thumbsup:
